title: MLB Count Leverage
headline_insight: Fall behind 3-0 and the pitcher almost always reaches for the heater: on a 3-0 count a four-seam fastball is the pitch 65.12% of the time, thrown in the strike zone 62.93% of the time.
what_it_means: Count state strongly shapes what gets thrown. In a must-throw-a-strike 3-0 hole the four-seam share (65.12%) roughly doubles its ~30% share in even and ahead counts, and the in-zone rate climbs because the hitter usually is not swinging. As the pitcher gets ahead the mix broadens toward sliders and changeups and the in-zone rate drops.
how_to_read: The chart shows pitch-type mix by count-leverage class; the table breaks it down to each exact ball-strike count. Every rate is over its own non-null denominator, not the raw class count.
why_it_matters: It is a clean descriptive baseline for how leverage drives pitch selection over 693,037 pitches, useful context before any modeling.
caveat: DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY over the local 2025 Statcast pull; the type==S strike rate conflates called, swinging and foul strikes (no per-pitch swing/take in this corpus). Not a predictor; no edge or ROI claim.
